Name: Registrations
Summary: Sign-ups for events or other subjects: places, prices and a deadline, a confirmation e-mail with a personal code, and a page where visitors look up or cancel their registration.
Guide:
An instance is usually linked to an Events instance, so editors open registration per event. Without that link, editors add their own subjects, such as a course, by ID. The module takes no payments: it shows the editors' payment link, and editors mark registrations as paid.

Add it to the site

app.Use(
    events.Module("agenda", "Agenda"),
    registrations.Module("signup", "Sign-ups", registrations.ForEvents("agenda")),
)

The key (signup) is used in the admin, in form actions and in the template functions, and must be unique on the site. The title (Sign-ups) is what editors see in the admin and the page editor.

  • ForEvents("agenda") links the instance to that Events instance. Editors pick its events in the admin, e-mail names the event and when it takes place, and registration closes when the event starts unless editors set a deadline. Add the Events instance as well.
  • Currency("GBP") sets the currency of the prices; the default is EUR. It must be an ISO 4217 code, or the app does not start.

Without ForEvents, editors add subjects in the admin with an ID (letters, digits, -, _, . and :, up to 64 characters) and a name. Templates pass that ID wherever they would pass an event's .ID.

With ForEvents, an event's page also tells search engines about its registration. The Events module gives the page a schema.org Event in its structured data, which core's head tags write with {{structuredData}}, and this module adds an Offer to it as offers: the price per adult, such as "12.50", or "0.00" when it is free, the currency, the event's page as url, InStock while visitors can register or SoldOut when every place is taken, and as validThrough the time registration closes, the event's start unless editors set a deadline. An event without registration settings, and registration that is switched off or past its deadline while places are left, give no offer. See Search and SEO.

Show the sign-up form

The registrationForm component renders the sign-up box of one subject. On an event page (agenda/event.gohtml or events/event.gohtml):

{{registrationForm "signup" .ID}}

It shows the prices, the places left, the deadline, the result of the visitor's last post and the form, or a notice when the subject is full or closed. When the instance is placed on a page, it also links to the lookup page. A subject without registration settings renders nothing, so the line can stay in the template of every event.

A theme changes the markup with signup/form.gohtml for this instance, or registrations/form.gohtml for every instance. Generate the default to start from, together with the other templates and e-mails of the instance:

task templates -- signup

The default uses wt-registration classes with the shared wt-form, wt-notice and wt-button, laid out by the optional stylesheet webthings.css, which the layout links with {{styles "webthings.css" "site.css"}} (see The base stylesheet). Its texts go through tl, so the site's translations apply.

To write the form in the template itself, registration returns the subject's availability in the page's language:

{{with registration "signup" .ID}}
    <section id="signup">
        {{with .Notes}}<div class="notes">{{.}}</div>{{end}}
        {{if .Open}}
            {{form_open .Form}}
                {{form_field .Form "subject" nil}}
                {{form_field .Form "name" nil}}
                {{form_field .Form "email" nil}}
                {{form_field .Form "adults" nil}}
                {{if .AllowChildren}}{{form_field .Form "children" nil}}{{end}}
                {{form_field .Form "notes" nil}}
                <button>Sign up</button>
            {{form_close}}
            {{if .Capacity}}<p>{{.Left}} places left</p>{{end}}
        {{else if .Full}}<p>This event is full.</p>
        {{else if .Configured}}<p>Registration is closed.</p>{{end}}
    </section>
{{end}}

Configured is set once editors saved settings for the subject. Open is set while registration is switched on, the deadline has not passed and places are left. Prices are amounts in cents: {{money .Prices.Adult .Currency}} shows them in the page's language. Notes are the editors' notes for registrants, rendered from Markdown with their own paragraphs, so they go in a <div> rather than a <p>.

.Form is the sign-up form: form_open writes the form tag, posting to .Action, with the spam trap and the page to return to, the element whose id is the instance key. form_field renders one of its fields by its key, with its label and limits, translated with the site's translations and in the site's form theme; the ids start with the key, such as signup-name. subject is a hidden field with the subject's ID, adults start at 1, and while places are limited adults and children each go up to .Left, at most 50. See Template functions. Inputs written by hand with the field names work too.

Visitors

The form posts to /_/signup/register (.Action, or {{registerURL "signup"}} anywhere) with the fields of registrations.SignupInput, plus the spam trap and the page to return to that form_open adds.

Field
subject the subject ID, such as the event's .ID (required)
name, email required; the name on one line
adults 1 when missing or empty
children 0 when missing; refused unless editors allow children
notes optional remarks, up to 2000 characters

One sign-up takes at most 50 places, and sign-ups that arrive at the same moment never exceed the capacity. The registration keeps the language of the page the form was on.

After signing up, the visitor gets a confirmation e-mail with a code such as K7Q4-9M2X. When the instance is placed on a page, the visitor then lands on the registration's own page with ?signup=registered; otherwise back on the form's page with ?signup=registered&code=K7Q4-9M2X. Other results return to the form's page:

?signup= Meaning
full not enough places left
closed registration is not open
invalid a field is missing or wrong, such as a number of places that is not a number
throttled too many posts: a visitor may send 10 sign-ups or cancellations per 10 minutes

With invalid or full, the form shows the visitor's answers again, with a message in the page's language at each field to correct. The component and form_field do this without a change to the template; inputs written by hand do not. Of several sign-up forms on one page, only the one for the subject the visitor chose shows them. See A post with mistakes. A sign-up or cancellation that fails for another reason, such as an unreachable database, gets the site's error page, 500.gohtml.

{{registrationResult "signup"}} reads the result and {{registrationCode "signup"}} the code; the component shows both. Posts that fill in the spam trap are answered with registered and stored nowhere. Visitors are told apart by IP address, so list a reverse proxy in Config.TrustedProxies. A post that stores nothing, spam, invalid, full, closed or throttled, leaves the pages in the site's output cache as they are; see Modules and the output cache.

The registration page

Place the instance on a page to let visitors look up and cancel their registration. With the page at /en/registration:

Address Template Shows
/en/registration signup/lookup.gohtml a form asking for the code
/en/registration/<code> signup/registration.gohtml one registration with its cancel form

registrations/<name>.gohtml serves every instance without a design of its own. The lookup page gets a registrations.LookupView. Its .Form is the form of registrations.LookupInput, sent to .Action with method GET as ?code=, with the code field's id registration-code:

{{/* @dot github.com/donseba/go-webthings/modules/registrations.LookupView */}}
<h1>{{.Title}}</h1>
{{if .NotFound}}<p>No registration has the code {{.Code}}.</p>{{end}}

{{form_open .Form}}
    {{form_field .Form "code" nil}}
    <button>Look up</button>
{{form_close}}

A code typed in lowercase, with spaces or without the dash lands on the right address. Every answer below the page, "not found" for an unknown code included, is sent with Cache-Control: private, no-store and X-Robots-Tag: noindex, so neither Stats nor the missed paths of Redirects record a code. Cancelling needs the code and the e-mail address used to sign up, the fields of registrations.CancelInput:

{{/* @dot github.com/donseba/go-webthings/modules/registrations.RegistrationView */}}
<h1>{{.Subject.Title}}</h1>
<p>{{.Code}} · {{.Name}} · {{.Adults}} adults{{if .Total}} · {{money .Total .Currency}}{{end}}</p>
{{with .PaymentLink}}<p>Please pay using: {{.}}</p>{{end}}
{{with .Info}}<div class="notes">{{.}}</div>{{end}}

<section id="{{.Key}}">
    {{if eq .Result "cancelled"}}<p>Your registration is cancelled.</p>{{end}}
    {{if eq .Result "invalid"}}<p>That e-mail address does not match this registration.</p>{{end}}
    {{if not .Cancelled}}
        {{form_open .Form}}
            {{form_field .Form "code" nil}}
            {{form_field .Form "email" nil}}
            <button>Cancel registration</button>
        {{form_close}}
    {{end}}
</section>

Here .Notes are the visitor's own remarks, as plain text, and .Info the editors' notes for registrants, rendered from Markdown. .Subject.When is when the event takes place, a frontend.When as an event's .When gives it, so the partial of the Events README shows it too; it is zero for a subject that is no event (.Subject.When.IsZero). The starting point from task templates -- signup shows it as that partial does: an event over several days with a time as "date, time – date, time", such as "Monday 16 November 2026, 09:00 – Tuesday 17 November 2026, 18:00". .Form is the cancel form, with the code as a hidden field; it returns the visitor to the element whose id is .Key, the instance key. After invalid, it shows the address the visitor typed again, as the sign-up form does.

Cancelling frees the places and sends a cancellation e-mail. An unpaid registration gets the payment status cancelled; a paid one stays paid, so it can be refunded.

In the admin

Each instance has its own section (/admin/signup; /admin is the default admin path). The overview lists the subjects with their status (open, closed or full), registrations and places taken. With ForEvents it lists every event of the agenda; without it, New subject adds one.

A subject's Settings hold:

  • Open for registration, the number of Places (adults and children together; 0 is unlimited) and Registration closes, in the site's timezone.
  • Price per adult and, when Children can be registered, Price per child, typed as 12.50 or 12,50.
  • Per language, the Notes for registrants in Markdown, shown with the form, on the registration page and in the confirmation, and a Payment link (a payment URL or bank details), shown while payment is pending.

The subject's page lists its registrations, cancelled ones included, with the totals and Export CSV. A registration with a total starts as pending. Editors change its payment status, add admin notes, cancel it or move it to the trash; cancelling in the admin sends no e-mail. Move to trash moves a registration to the trash and frees its places; a restored registration keeps its code, and restoring is refused when too few places are left by then. Editors' rights are set per instance in the groups' permission matrix; Export CSV needs the export right (see Groups and the matrix). In the export, a value that starts with =, +, - or @ gets a leading apostrophe, so a spreadsheet shows it as text instead of running it as a formula.

E-mail

Two mail templates, sent to the visitor in the language of the page they signed up on:

  • confirmation, after signing up: the code, the event's date and time, the places, the total, the payment link, the notes for registrants as the Markdown editors wrote (.Info), and a link to the registration page when the instance is on a page.
  • cancellation, after cancelling on the site.

The confirmation shows when the event takes place as the starting point of the registration page does, so an event over several days with a time as "date, time – date, time". Replies go to the site's e-mail address from Site settings. A theme replaces the texts with mail/signup/<name>.gohtml or mail/registrations/<name>.gohtml. A mail that cannot be sent is logged; the registration stands.

From Go

registrations.Of(app, "signup") returns the instance once the app has started, for example to open registration for an event from seed data:

signup := registrations.Of(app, "signup")

err := signup.SaveSettings(ctx, registrations.Settings{
    SubjectID:  eventID,
    Open:       true,
    Capacity:   40,
    AdultPrice: 1250, // 12.50
    Texts:      []registrations.SubjectText{{Locale: "en", Notes: "Doors open at **19:30**."}},
})

Notes are Markdown, as editors write them in the admin.

Availability, Registrations and Summaries read the sign-ups, and ByCode finds one by its code. Register signs someone up with the same checks as the form, but sends no e-mail, and Cancel cancels a registration, freeing its places. Delete, Undelete and Purge move a registration to the trash, bring it back or remove it for good. What SaveSettings, Register, Cancel, Delete and Undelete change, such as the places left, shows on the site at once, also on pages in the site's output cache; see Modules and the output cache.

Related modules

  • Events holds the events visitors sign up for.
  • Forms collects other questions from visitors, with an inbox.

Funcs.Name: registrationCode
Funcs.Doc: code is the visitor's registration code after registering on a page when the instance is placed on no page of its own, for example {{with registrationCode "signup"}}<p>Your code: {{.}}</p>{{end}}; "" otherwise.

Funcs.Name: registrationForm
Funcs.Doc: registrationForm renders the form component of a subject, for example {{registrationForm "signup" .ID}} on an event page. Subjects without registration settings render nothing.

SQL.Name: postgres
SQL.SQL:
-- Settings per subject (usually an event) that visitors can register for.
-- Prices are in cents. Without closes_at, registration for an event closes
-- when it starts. What registrants read (notes, payment link) is per
-- language in wt_registration_subject_text.
CREATE TABLE wt_registration_subject (
    instance       VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    subject_id     VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    title          VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    is_open        BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    capacity       INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    closes_at      TIMESTAMPTZ,
    adult_price    BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    child_price    BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    allow_children BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    created_at     TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    created_by     UUID,
    updated_at     TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    updated_by     UUID,
    PRIMARY KEY (instance, subject_id)
);

-- The notes for registrants and the payment link of a subject per language.
CREATE TABLE wt_registration_subject_text (
    instance     VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    subject_id   VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    locale       VARCHAR(35) NOT NULL,
    notes        TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    payment_link VARCHAR(500) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    PRIMARY KEY (instance, subject_id, locale),
    FOREIGN KEY (instance, subject_id) REFERENCES wt_registration_subject (instance, subject_id) ON DELETE CASCADE
);

-- Registrations are visitor submissions; cancelled ones are kept with
-- cancelled_at set and no longer take places. Deleted ones are in the
-- admin's trash (deleted_at) and take no places either. Codes stay unique
-- in the trash too, so a restored registration keeps its code.
CREATE TABLE wt_registration (
    id             UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    instance       VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    subject_id     VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    code           VARCHAR(9) NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    name           VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    email          VARCHAR(254) NOT NULL,
    adults         INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    children       INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    total          BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    payment_status VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'none',
    notes          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    admin_notes    TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    locale         VARCHAR(35) NOT NULL,
    created_at     TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    created_by     UUID,
    updated_at     TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    updated_by     UUID,
    deleted_at     TIMESTAMPTZ,
    deleted_by     UUID,
    cancelled_at   TIMESTAMPTZ
);

CREATE INDEX wt_registration_subject_list ON wt_registration (instance, subject_id, created_at);

    subject_id     VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    code           VARCHAR(9) NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    name           VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    email          VARCHAR(254) NOT NULL,
    adults         INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    children       INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    total          BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    payment_status VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'none',
    notes          TEXT NOT NULL,
    admin_notes    TEXT NOT NULL,
    locale         VARCHAR(35) NOT NULL,
    created_at     DATETIME(6) NOT NULL,
    created_by     VARCHAR(36) NULL,
    updated_at     DATETIME(6) NOT NULL,
    updated_by     VARCHAR(36) NULL,
    deleted_at     DATETIME(6) NULL,
    deleted_by     VARCHAR(36) NULL,
    cancelled_at   DATETIME(6) NULL,
    INDEX wt_registration_subject_list (instance, subject_id, created_at)
) ENGINE=InnoDB;

Tables.Name: wt_registration_subject
Tables.Note: Settings per subject (usually an event) that visitors can register for. Prices are in cents. Without closes_at, registration for an event closes when it starts. What registrants read (notes, payment link) is per language in wt_registration_subject_text.

Tables.Name: wt_registration_subject_text
Tables.Note: The notes for registrants and the payment link of a subject per language.
Indexes: FOREIGN KEY (instance, subject_id) REFERENCES wt_registration_subject (instance, subject_id) ON DELETE CASCADE

Tables.Name: wt_registration
Tables.Note: Registrations are visitor submissions; cancelled ones are kept with cancelled_at set and no longer take places. Deleted ones are in the admin's trash (deleted_at) and take no places either. Codes stay unique in the trash too, so a restored registration keeps its code.

Types.Name: Availability
Types.Doc: Availability tells templates whether and how visitors can register for a subject.

Types.Name: CancelInput
Types.Doc: CancelInput is the cancel form a visitor posts to /_/<key>/cancel: the registration's code and the e-mail address it was made with.

Types.Name: Cents
Types.Doc: Cents is an amount of money in hundredths, for example 1250 for 12.50. Templates show it with money, for example {{money .Total .Currency}}.
Types.Decl: type Cents int64

Types.Name: Fact
Types.Doc: Fact is one setting in the summary; Label is translated.

Types.Name: FormView
Types.Doc: FormView is the data of the form component: whether and how visitors can register for a subject, with the result of the visitor's last post.

Types.Name: LookupInput
Types.Doc: LookupInput is the lookup form, LookupView.Form: the code from the confirmation, sent with method get as ?code=. Its field's id is registration-code.

Types.Name: LookupView
Types.Doc: LookupView is the data of registrations/lookup.gohtml: a form where visitors enter their code.

Types.Name: MailView
Types.Doc: MailView is the data of the mail templates confirmation and cancellation, in the language the visitor registered in.

Types.Name: NewSubjectView
Types.Doc: NewSubjectView adds a subject that is not an event.

Types.Name: OverviewRow
Types.Doc: OverviewRow is one event or subject in the overview, with its number of registrations and the places taken, out of the capacity when there is one.

Types.Name: OverviewView
Types.Doc: OverviewView lists the subjects with their registrations.

Types.Name: PaymentStatus
Types.Doc: PaymentStatus tells whether a registration was paid.

Types.Name: Prices
Types.Doc: Prices are the prices per place.

Types.Name: Registration
Types.Doc: Registration is one sign-up.

Types.Name: RegistrationAdminView
Types.Doc: RegistrationAdminView shows one registration to editors.

Types.Name: RegistrationRow
Types.Doc: RegistrationRow is one registration in the list of an event or subject; Cancelled registrations stay in the list.
Types.Decl:
type RegistrationRow struct {
	URL       string
	Code      string
	Name      string
	Email     string
	Adults    int
	Children  int
	Total     string
	Payment   string
	Date      string
	Cancelled bool
}

Types.Name: RegistrationView
Types.Doc: RegistrationView is the data of registrations/registration.gohtml.

Types.Name: Service
Types.Doc: Service is one Registrations instance, for the website's own code.

Types.Name: Settings
Types.Doc: Settings decide whether and how visitors can register for one subject.

Types.Name: SettingsView
Types.Doc: SettingsView edits the settings of a subject.

Types.Name: Signup
Types.Doc: Signup is what a visitor submits.
Types.Decl:
type Signup struct {
	SubjectID string
	Name      string
	Email     string
	Adults    int
	Children  int
	Notes     string
	Locale    string
}

Types.Name: SignupInput
Types.Doc: SignupInput is the sign-up form a visitor posts to /_/<key>/register: the subject, a name, an e-mail address, the number of adults (1 when empty) and children, and remarks. Themes render its fields with form_field, with their limits (Availability.Form), or write inputs with these names.
Types.Decl:
type SignupInput struct {
	Subject  string `form:"input,hidden" name:"subject"  required:"true" maxLength:"64"   pattern:"^[A-Za-z0-9_.:\\-]+$"`
	Name     string `form:"input,text"   name:"name"     required:"true" maxLength:"200"                                 label:"Name"           line:"true" autocomplete:"name"`
	Email    string `form:"input,email"  name:"email"    required:"true" maxLength:"254"                                 label:"E-mail address"             autocomplete:"email" validate:"mail"`
	Adults   int    `form:"input,number" name:"adults"                                                                   label:"Adults"                                                          min:"1" max:"50"`
	Children int    `form:"input,number" name:"children"                                                                 label:"Children"                                                        min:"0" max:"50"`
	Notes    string `form:"textarea"     name:"notes"                    maxLength:"2000"                                label:"Remarks"                                                                          placeholder:"Allergies, accessibility, questions…"`
}

Types.Name: Subject
Types.Doc: Subject is what visitors register for, as the admin and e-mail show it.

Types.Name: SubjectText
Types.Doc: SubjectText is what registrants of a subject read in one language.

Types.Name: SubjectView
Types.Doc: SubjectView shows one subject and its registrations.

Types.Name: Summary
Types.Doc: Summary counts the active registrations of one subject.
